zones.name: Core Ops

insights: High coupling (0.71) — 3 imports target "core"

The 0.71 coupling is one-directional grounding, not entanglement: all three files (log.ts, undo.ts, types.ts) depend only on foundational modules — graph/graph.ts, schema/schema.ts, mutations/types.ts — and none of those foundational files import back from ops/, so core-ops sits cleanly above core-schema/core-mutations in a layered DAG despite the zone-level bidirectional crossing count (core→core-ops 12, core-ops→core 3).

All three ops files are re-exported directly from packages/core/src/index.ts alongside the rest of core's public surface (OperationLog, checkUndo, undoPrimitives, Author/Batch/Operation types) — the ops/ directory is an internal grouping within one package's barrel, not a separately consumable module boundary, so the zone split is organizational rather than architectural.

cli/check/*.ts (beginnings, brand, city, context, fields, intelligence, policy, relations, migrations, routes, settings, modules, lenses) each import directly from internal submodules — schema/schema.ts, mutations/{derive-edits,node-ref,decidable}.ts, permissions/policy.ts, theme/{derive,kit,types}.ts, city.ts, beginning.ts, schema/{figures,define-node}.ts — by relative path rather than through a single check-facing seam or core's own index.ts barrel. The checker suite therefore has no boundary from core internals: renaming or moving any of those ~9 internal modules ripples across every check/*.ts file individually, and the 'core-cli → core: 15 imports' crossing is really many independent point-to-point reaches rather than one interface.

Consumers of core-ops (store.ts, persistence/{sqlite,memory,types}.ts, permissions/types.ts, sync/types.ts) sit strictly downstream — no file inside ops/ imports any of them back — so despite the high raw coupling number the dependency shape is a clean, acyclic layer rather than a leak.
